newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB confident on continuing wheat exports to Iran.
newsitem.headline: AWB confident on continuing wheat exports to Iran.

text.p: Australian Wheat Board (AWB) chairman Trevor Flugge said on Wednesday he was confident the political crisis with Iran would not affect Australia's A$500 million a year wheat exports to the country.
On Iran, Flugge said he was very confident political differences with Australia would be kept separate from commercial issues.
"Both sides would be reluctant to put trade in jeporady," he said in response to a question from Reuters.
"I am comfortable and confident that its not going to affect us," he said.
Australia is exporting two to three million tonnes of wheat to Iran this year (1996/97), valued at about A$500 million.

Not all of the wheat contracted for by Iran has been delivered, leaving questions over whether Iran might follow with cancellations of unshipped tonnages in retaliation for Australia's withdrawl of its ambassador from Tehran last weekend.
He was withdrawn in response to the German court verdict last week which which accused Iran's leaders of ordering the 1992 murder of four Kurdish dissidents.
Flugge on wednesday pointed out that Iran was not the only wheat customer of Australia where political issues arose.
He praised Australian Prime Minister John Howard's handling of political discussions with China as showing consciousness of trade sensitivity.
Major problems with China could have arisen if Howard had not taken the right approach, Flugge said.
